 Tesla Stocks Rise 5.34% After Barclays Lifts Target to $450
 Less than 1 min read TSLA Tesla, the electric-vehicle and autonomy developer TSLA , rose 5.34% to $392.09 in Monday's regular session, extending its advance from 9:50 a.m. ET. Barclays gave investors a fresh reason to buy: Barron's reported that the bank upgraded the shares and lifted its price target to $450 from $370. That leaves roughly 14.8% upside to the target after the rally. 
 The operating numbers still demand attention. Tesla reported third-quarter results showing revenue of approximately $28.0 billion. Automotive revenue slipped 3% to about $20.6 billion, while capital spending reached roughly $4.7 billion. Its quarterly filing puts expected 2026 capital expenditures above $20 billion, including investments in computing infrastructure, manufacturing and research facilities. 
 The valuation leaves little room for weak execution: shares sit 11.51% above the $351.62 GF Value estimate. Barclays' higher target supports the bullish case, but it cannot fund the expansion. The next test is whether vehicle sales, autonomy revenue and manufacturing efficiency can generate enough operating cash to support the spending push. Investors need evidence that those investments can produce durable cash flow before treating the remaining target upside as an easy gain.
